title: Credits · Catnet Systems
text: Credits a production kittyn Creator & Creative Director Game design, world direction, and production of SpookCo: Last Stop — a cooperative horror world for VRChat. Music composition & production. How SpookCo is made Our original props, environment kits and characters are modeled procedurally in Blender using Python. UVs are unwrapped and packed into texture atlases, with baked ambient occlusion, edge highlights and color gradients forming the base of SpookCo's signature hand-painted style. All ten spook characters have editable Rigify rigs and skinned meshes, using biped rigs for the humanoid cast and a quadruped rig for the Hound. Character-specific animations are baked for Unity and driven by a shared animation controller. Unity C# editor build scripts generate world geometry, place assets and wire up gameplay interactions. The game's logic is written in UdonSharp for VRChat. Our original art assets and editable Blender sources, together with texture atlases, UV layouts and painting guides, are currently under review for release on the official SpookCo website, for artists and anyone interested in learning how the world is made. Shopkeeper character The warehouse shopkeeper uses Rusk (Quest version) by komado / こまど , from あまとうさぎ . Original model on BOOTH . The shopkeeper's local animations and world integration were created for SpookCo. Platform & development tools Platform: VRChat SDK and UdonSharp. Development tools: Blender, Clip Studio Paint, Affinity, Codex, and Ableton Live. Lighting: VRC Light Volumes by RED_SIM (MIT) carries the crew's flashlight beams through the world's surface shaders. Particles and grass: GPU Particle Volumes, GPU Snow, and GPU Infinite Grass by RED_SIM ; GPU Rain Particle by nekochanfood / ちゃんふー堂 . Autumn leaves, motes, ground weather, and gathering behavior use original SpookCo shaders and models. In-world fonts: Noto Sans JP from the Noto CJK project supports English and Japanese UI under the SIL Open Font License; its license ships with the world. Liberation Sans, supplied through TextMesh Pro, is also credited in the world's Credits page with its complete font license. The website uses system fonts. Its night-shift illustration is original SVG artwork, not a gameplay screenshot. Shader acknowledgments VRChat and Xiexe: Toon shading uses VRChat's Mobile/Toon Lit, based in part on XSToon by Xiexe, with additional modifications for SpookCo. Unity Technologies: Additional shader components are based on Unity's built-in shaders. RED_SIM: The Depot Surface and Fogged Toon Lit shaders include the VRC Light Volumes shader library (MIT), which draws the flashlight beams. David Hoskins and David A. Roberts: The Depot Surface grain helper uses Hash without Sine, with an HLSL adaptation based on Roberts's MIT-licensed publication. Read the complete shader copyright and license notices . Music The SpookCo soundtrack uses original compositions, arrangements, and synthesized sounds, together with samples from Ableton's Core Library . Thanks to Ableton and its sound-content licensors. Ableton Live is used for music development and auditioning. Core Library content retains Ableton's proprietary terms; it is not CC0. Earlier, uninstalled palette studies used Retro Synths by Puremagnetik and Mood Reel by Ableton and its contributing sound designers . These are development acknowledgments; those Packs are not sources in the currently installed soundtrack. Read the music source acknowledgments and license references . Weather audio Spawn weather uses Rain (loopable) by Ylmir , Rain in the Gutter Loop by Ogrebane , and wind1 by Luke.RUSTLTD . These sources are CC0 1.0 ; credit is retained voluntarily. The sounds are edited and layered for the world. Warehouse reflections use original SpookCo processing, and spectral air is original SpookCo synthesis. TinyWorlds' recordings are still used in player footsteps. Their leaf sounds were removed from the weather mix; this courtesy acknowledgment also preserves that earlier contribution. Read the complete weather sound notices . Outdoor wildlife uses crow recordings by IgnasD, owl recordings by Breviceps, distant dog recordings by Brandon Morris (submitted by HaelDB), and a black-capped chickadee recording by nfrae. These sources use CC0 1.0, with voluntary creator credit retained. The recordings are trimmed, filtered, softened and placed at a distance for the world; the softer spectral air is original SpookCo synthesis. Read the wildlife source links and modification details . Other sound effects The world also includes third-party ambient, footstep, creature, and interface sounds. The complete sound-effect notices retain the individual authors, source links, CC BY attribution, CC0 acknowledgments, and modification details. The van departure uses Big diesel engine (#0967) by Joseph SARDIN / BigSoundBank. The source is CC0 1.0 ; credit is retained voluntarily. The recording is edited for the world, and the departure beep is original SpookCo synthesis. Read the van departure sound notices . Inspiration SpookCo draws on short-round horror and scavenging games. No characters, models, audio, or code from Terrors of Nowhere or SlashCo are included. Ready to clock in? Start with the player guide or return to SpookCo: Last Stop .

title: About SpookCo
text: About SpookCo SpookCo is a night maintenance company. This page covers who you work for, what the work is and what else is on site. The rest of the field guide covers getting home. The work SpookCo holds the maintenance contracts nobody else will take. When a site's caretaker stops answering invoices, the contract goes to auction and SpookCo bids. The contracts were inexpensive. The reason is on site. A contract pays while the equipment runs and company property is accounted for. That is the whole business. So every night a crew drives out, starts the generators (maintenance performed), brings the cargo back (property accounted for) and leaves before departure. Company property means the cargo cases, the generators, the lantern and the van. All contracts are night contracts. There is no day shift. Dispatch and the auction Dispatch is Precast Unit 03, at the end of Canal Street. It is the only SpookCo building. It was bought at auction with its contents: one van, one trailer, one red hurricane lantern and a box of letterhead already printed SPOOKCO. The buyer kept the name. Reprinting costs money. The office has a desk, a lamp and a phone. Management signs every contract. Management remains at dispatch. Nobody has seen Management at dispatch. Questions may be left in writing. Spooks Every site had staff. Every staff member had a job. The job did not end. Whatever is still on a site is called a spook. Spooks keep to their old duties: the paths are swept, the calls are connected, the property is guarded. Being on duty is what makes them dangerous. They are not angry. They are thorough. Spooks keep out of the lantern's light and leave the van alone. The only explanation on file is that the lantern is company property, and spooks respect company property. The lantern is the only company property that has never gone missing. After an escape, spooks return to the field. They have rounds to make. For warnings, senses and escape routes, see Know the spooks . Home sites Three spooks have a home site on file: The Groundskeeper belongs to Camp Deadwood. Roadkill belongs to Last Chance Service Station. The Switchboard belongs to Calder Nuclear Laboratory. Briarwood's records are incomplete. All three still turn up everywhere. SpookCo buys its contracts in bundles, and staff on one contract count as staff on every site in the bundle. Management considers this efficient. Most spooks have no home site at all. They go wherever the work is, and at night the work is wherever SpookCo is. Company vocabulary Word Meaning spook Whatever is on a site. crew The employees on a contract, also called the night crew. This includes you. dispatch Precast Unit 03, at the end of Canal Street. The only SpookCo building, and the voice on paper. Management The signature on every contract. Remains at dispatch. retained The company word for an employee who missed departure. Retained employees are not listed as absent. departure The van leaving the site. It leaves on schedule.

title: Controls & accessibility
text: Controls & accessibility Use the Controls & Accessibility panel beside dispatch’s ready board. You can also reach it from the van and personal inventory. Preferences are saved separately for desktop, VR, and touch. The Controls side rail groups them into Input & Interaction , Menu , Placement & HUD , Flashlight , Audio , and Language . It shows settings relevant to your current input device and remembers your last category during the session. Choose your language On a first visit, the game waits for your saved profile, then shows a bilingual English/Japanese picker if no supported language is saved. On desktop, press 1 for English or 2 for Japanese in that initial picker, or hold Tab and click. In VR, use the personal-menu pointer on the floating picker. Change it later under Controls → Language . The choice is saved across visits and shared between your desktop and VR profiles; resetting controls does not reset language. It changes only your own view, so the crew can use different languages. Website language links do not change your in-world setting. Branding, legal notices, and developer diagnostics retain their original text. Desktop: keep chase actions on keys Action Default Temporary Inventory peek Hold Tab ; release to close, unless Menu is set to keep it open Reopen your last selected page I ; press again to close Keep a temporary Tab page open Press I while it is visible Click a menu already kept open Hold Tab ; the current page stays selected Flashlight F Draw reusable equipment 1 Draw equipped consumable 2 Stow personal item 3 Select reserve 1 / 2 4 / 5 Drop task cargo 6 Use drawn item Native Use action / Use button Collect or interact Targeted world interaction / context action A Tab peek does not replace the page remembered by I. For example, close Controls, peek at Inventory with Tab, then press I: Controls returns to the category you selected. Holding Tab on an already open menu enables clicking without changing pages. Shift+Tab also opens the menu while sprint is held; Alt/Control chords are ignored. Native cursor and movement behavior remains controlled by VRChat. The six numbered shortcuts work without Tab, including with Shift held. They can be rebound, and conflicting bindings are reported. Reserve selection swaps the chosen reserve into the equipped slot; it does not draw or consume it. Press 2 to draw, then make a fresh Use input. Choose Controls → Menu → When Tab is released to close it or keep it open. If you bind an item action to I, that binding takes precedence and the menu hint omits I. VR: wrist or floating panel Flick the right stick up or down to put the next item in your hand: hands free, your gear, then each consumable you carry. Pull the trigger on that hand to use it. Nothing needs confirming and no menu needs opening. At dispatch, hold the stick up to ready up or unready: a three second count appears across your view and letting go early cancels it ( Controls → Input & Interaction → Ready hold turns this back into a quick half-second hold). Hold the stick down for about half a second to open the menu. If your controller's stick does not register up or down, hold the jump button for about half a second instead: it opens and closes the same menu, whose READY / JOIN button readies you up, and the ready post by the ramp does the same by touch. The first time you arrive at dispatch in VR, a short banner across your view says so. Choose either wrist and either equipment hand. There is no button on the wrist, and opening the menu does not freeze movement. Floating mode is the default. The panel appears once, level in front of you, at the moment you open it, and switching tabs never moves it again. If you open it while looking up at a sign or down at the floor it slides toward where you are looking, and it pulls in front of any wall or board closer than its set distance. The first time it opens for you, a short banner across your view says where it is. Wrist mode instead keeps the panel attached to your chosen wrist, so it travels with your arm. Its height, distance, size and angle are set on the Placement & HUD page (a category on the Controls rail; see below), and Aim at me there turns it to face your eyes from wherever you are holding your hand: hold your arm the way you read it and press it with the other hand. All of it is saved with your profile. The floating panel closes itself when you move more than three metres from where it was placed, when the expedition starts, when you pick up cargo, and when you take a hit or go down. If it ends up out of reach, close it with the same stick or jump hold and open it again: a fresh panel appears in front of you. Aim at me on the Placement / HUD page does the same. Menus cannot be opened during transit between stops. Buttons that duplicate VRChat's own controls are hidden unless the current situation needs them, so the panel stays compact. The status readout card (the round, your cash, health and level, anything acting on you (soda, Adrenaline, slowed, fog, EMF bearing) and what is in your hand, on up to five lines) sits small in the lower-left corner of your view during a trip (the briefing, the stop and the van ride): about a metre ahead, following your head's turn with a slight lag and pulled in front of walls. At dispatch it rides your wrist instead and stays hidden unless Controls → Menu → Wrist display at dispatch is shown. An alert brings it up anywhere and turns the card red. On the wrist it steps aside while the menu is open on the same wrist. Choose Placement & HUD → Wrist readout → Size to set the card's size. Placement & HUD (a category on the Controls rail, office board or menu) moves things to where you can see them, one element at a time: the menu panel, the wrist readout, the item in your hand, the alert banner and the hand torch. Pick the element with Next element , the axis with Next axis (offset, tilt, size, or a HUD cell), and step it with - / + ; the page shows the numbers as you go, and while it is open the readout (and the item or torch you are placing) stays visible, even at dispatch (on the wrist it stays off beside a wrist-mode menu, where the card would cover the page). Next anchor cycles the readout between AUTO (the default: the HUD corner during a trip, your wrist at dispatch), HEAD (HUD) everywhere and WRIST everywhere. On AUTO the page shows and moves the corner spot (keep your head at the page's centre to see the card beside it), and WRIST lets you set the wrist pose. For the held item it switches hand / head, and for the menu panel floating / wrist. Pinned elements sit in a cell of a 9 x 7 grid about a metre ahead, pull in front of walls, trail your head's turn a little ( HUD follow locks them instead) and on PC hide while VRChat's camera is out; the HUD frame element sets how wide and tall that grid is. The alert banner always trails. Your item placement is only for you: other players still see items in the normal hand pose. On desktop the VR-only elements say so, and the HUD frame is the desktop HUD scale ; on touch you place the alert banner. Reset element and Reset all placement put things back; everything is saved with your profile for each input type. Personal items follow the chosen hand. Cargo uses normal pickup controls, or the accessible Carry / Drop actions. If a native pickup occupies the equipment hand, stow or move it deliberately; personal equipment must not forcibly release it. Generator controls and rescue In VR, tap the translucent rectangle on a generator control with either hand. Each tap performs one action; move your hand away before tapping again. Holding your hand in the control does not repeat it. Point-and-trigger also works, and desktop/touch players keep their normal point-and-select controls. Touch and trigger together count as one press. The flashing beacon identifies an unfueled generator. The nearby panel shows its fuel count: field generators need one can , industrial generators two . Once fueled, complete the shown startup task and press Start Engine . Instructions, meters, and feedback stay on the panel; there is no overhead generator label. Practice uses the same controls. Revives happen automatically when an eligible teammate stays close enough to a downed player. There is no held repair/rescue mode or Cancel repair button to configure. Flashlight Every crew member carries a light into the field. By default it is a head lamp that follows your gaze, so the beam lights whatever you look at, hands free. Controls → Flashlight adds a hand light on the right or left hand instead of, or as well as, the head lamp; in VR it points where that controller points, on desktop it follows your view. Both choices are saved with your profile. In VR, tap the trigger of your Light switch hand in the field to switch every beam you carry on or off. Controls → Flashlight → Light switch hand picks it: Other hand (the default, the hand that is not holding your equipment), Left trigger or Right trigger . If you pick your equipment hand, a tap switches the light only while no item is drawn; with an item out, that trigger uses the item. Holding a crate or gas can in the switch hand still lets you switch, and so does pointing an empty switch hand across something you are holding or carrying. With loot in one hand and a crate or gas can in the other, the loot hand's trigger stores the loot and the other trigger switches the light; with loot in your switch hand and the other hand free, the other trigger switches too while nothing is drawn in it. Storing loot never changes either hand setting. A held trigger does nothing to the light, and neither does a press that grabs, operates a generator or clicks a button, or any press while the menu is open. On desktop, F switches the light, and Controls → Flashlight → Flashlight power works everywhere. Lights are off at dispatch and come on when the stop begins; pressing a lamp button at dispatch previews your beams for a few seconds so you can see where they sit (only you see it; closing the menu keeps it, and it ends when you walk off, push a stick, change tab or open the menu again). In VR a hand light also puts a small torch in that hand, and in Controls → Flashlight , Hand beam orientation turns the beam 90 degrees out of the bottom (pinky side) or top (thumb side) of your fist so you can hold it at the shoulder (its offset moves the torch model, never the beam); desktop hand lights aim with your view and ignore the flip. Everyone in the instance sees everyone else's beams, and VR players' torches, including where a teammate is pointing. The switch makes an audible click-clack. Nearby players hear it, and so does a spook within earshot, much as it would hear a footstep. The Focused Beam perk (level 15) throws a narrower beam about two thirds farther, and its damped switch is quieter and silent to spooks. The Usher and Deadeye can still see its beam. Phone and tablet Use the screen’s MENU , USE ITEM , and COLLECT / INTERACT buttons. The world-space lobby boards are also present, but the screen controls are the intended touch shortcut. Inside inventory, select equipment, consumables, or reserves; use the separate Use action to activate the selected item. The iPhone build has been tried by the creator. Final touch layout and ergonomics still need broader device testing. Preferences and practice Accessible cargo carrying with the same reservation, penalty, delivery, and drop rules. Wrist/equipment handedness, the VR Light switch hand , the wrist HUD size, the ready hold count, and on the Placement & HUD page the placement of the menu panel, wrist readout, held item, alert banner and hand torch, plus the HUD frame (desktop: HUD scale). Audio (on the Controls rail): four levels, Main, SFX, Ambience and Music, each a slider with - / + buttons. 50% is the game as mixed, 100% adds a little headroom, 0% mutes; Main scales the other three. The levels are saved with your profile and shared by desktop, VR and touch, Reset controls & placement leaves them alone, and VRChat's own World volume still applies on top. Menu clicks follow the SFX level while you adjust it, and at dispatch a wind sample plays while the page is open so you can judge Ambience. Desktop key rebinding with conflict feedback and reset defaults. Separate persisted control profiles for each input family. Stick item select, on by default in VR: neutral deadzone 0.25, activation threshold 0.70, dwell 150 ms. Return to neutral before another step; each step equips outright. These settings control SpookCo actions, not VRChat’s native movement bindings. The free practice bay is open outside the roll-up door, on the right, with the lit generator guide boards across the yard fence in the vacant lot, facing the building; practice supplies spend no real items or cash. Generator tutorial progress is saved across visits; Reset tutorial clears that practice progress. A practice generator you finish clears away for you; the Reset tutorial post at the end of the practice bench (stand right at it and press twice) brings them all back. Walking out of the bay puts the practice supplies and crate back, and the shop always shows your real items. Selecting or collecting an item never activates it automatically. The lobby's two big boards stand in the dispatch office, front right of spawn. After you finish all three practice tasks, the training boards, Practice Bay sign, and Reset Tutorial sign/button dim together while you are away from the guide boards. Approaching the guide boards brightens them again; the reset button remains usable.

title: Equipment & field supplies
text: Equipment & field supplies Your inventory You have one reusable equipment slot , one equipped consumable , two reserve consumables , and one separate task-cargo slot . Duplicates are allowed; each occupies a slot. Purchases and scavenged supplies use the same three-slot pouch. Only one personal item is actively held at a time. Switching personal items does not discard cargo. Selecting a reserve swaps it with the equipped consumable. Collecting, selecting, and drawing do not automatically use an item; consuming one does not activate the next. On desktop, carried cargo and fuel use small HUD indicators, and the selected personal item appears as an icon with its name. These replace the obstructing first-person held models. Dropping cargo, docking fuel, using a consumable, or stowing an item clears the corresponding indicator. VR keeps normal hand models, and carried objectives remain visible to other players. Reusable equipment Unlocks require both a banked XP level and a lifetime commendation milestone. Commendations are not spent. Later equipment is deliberately a longer-term goal. Equipment Level Commendations Role Wind-up decoy 1 0 Place a distraction to pull the spook’s investigation away. Instant camera 4 12 A close-range flash can stun the spook; cooldowns and post-stun immunity limit repeated use. EMF pager 12 120 Passive proximity information about the spook. Trip alarm 18 400 Place one temporary alarm. A nearby spook triggers a positional signal and a brief stun; committed charges continue through it. Track shoes 24 1,200 Passive 10% movement bonus, within the shared bonus cap. Pager and shoes work without an active Use effect. Gear selection happens during shopping/loadout windows. Active gear has cooldowns; reconnecting or resetting must not refresh them. Cash consumables These prices and effects describe the current baseline and may be rebalanced. Supply Cash Effect Field ration 18 Restores one health when below your maximum. Sprint soda 16 +30% movement for 12 seconds, on top of the 20% cap shared by gear and perk bonuses. Not spent while a soda is already active. Rescue flare 22 Rescues a nearby downed teammate within 12 metres. Needs a valid teammate. Repair tape 20 Fixes one incomplete generator task step. You still press Start Engine yourself. Smoke canister 24 Ten seconds of visual concealment. Blocks spook sight through its cloud, but not hearing or attacks already in motion. Scrap bolt bundle 12 Toss a distraction onto nearby ground. Shares the decoy's resistance window; committed attacks ignore it. Door brace 18 Brace a nearby closed door for up to 45 seconds. Adds four seconds to one normal breach; charges break through. Opening the door removes it. Tool oil 20 Use beside an unfinished fueled generator for 25 seconds of easier startup controls and half the work-noise range. Flash bulb 24 One aimed camera-strength flash. Shares stun resistance with the camera and trip alarm. Emergency battery 28 Recharges your equipped active gear. Requires an active cooldown; an already armed trip alarm prevents recharging that alarm. The shop has three supply pages. Perks and consumables can complement each other: oil provides the same control assistance as Mechanic and combines with Silent Tools for quieter work, while a flash bulb provides a one-use alternative when your reusable slot holds something else. Smoke does not make you bulletproof or silence your movement. If the effect has no valid target, the request is rejected without spending the item. The shop guarantees a chosen supply, while field scavenging trades time and risk for a shared find. A repaired generator recharges active gear twice as fast within six metres , during work and extraction. Solid walls block its power, and multiple generators do not stack. A normal 30-second cooldown takes about 15 seconds if you stay connected; Quickdraw reduces that to about 12. The HUD and wrist show GENERATOR: GEAR RECHARGE 2x while connected. EMF and track shoes are passive, so they do not recharge. Power does not protect you from spooks or extend extraction. Selling Use Sell equipped consumable on the Shop page to sell the supply in your equipped slot. Selling is available in the same windows as buying, not in the field. Select it again within four seconds (or hold the button) to confirm. Bought supplies refund half their price; supplies found in the field refund a quarter and are marked (found) in your inventory. The Shop always sells your real equipped item. Practice supplies from the bay outside the depot never appear there, and they are put back when you leave the bay. Shared field loot Each stop rolls supplies at distinct authored locations. They are global pickups : once one player successfully collects an item, nobody else can collect that spawn. A full pouch shows Pouch Full and leaves it available. Starting participants Shared items 1 1–2 2 1–3 4 2–4 8 3–7 12 4–9 16 6–12 All ten cash consumables can appear, with duplicates allowed. Smoke, braces and oil are slightly less common than the original supplies; bulbs and batteries are rarer. Solo stop rolls omit the teammate-focused rescue flare. Supplies are optional: a contract never requires finding one. A pickup goes into the equipped consumable slot if empty, otherwise the first empty reserve. It is stored without being drawn. Collecting supplies awards no XP or cash. Unclaimed supplies disappear when the stop ends; collected supplies stay in your session pouch. Joins, host changes, restarts, and returning to dispatch do not reroll or replenish previously claimed supplies.

title: Dispatch FAQ
text: Dispatch FAQ Who makes SpookCo? SpookCo: Last Stop is a catnet systems production, created by kittyn , the Creator & Creative Director responsible for game design, world direction, and production. See the credits for the studio identity, development tools, and platform acknowledgments. Is this the finished game? No. SpookCo is still early in development and may change significantly after the game jam . The jam build is a working version, and its gameplay, progression, maps, and art are not final. Expect placeholder art and sound, changing balance, and unfinished edge cases. Spectator radar and AI diagnostics are development tools that may be removed. PC, Android/Quest, and iOS bundles have been built; broad device and multiplayer acceptance is still in progress. How many people can play? The implemented participant limit is 16 , and solo play is supported. Handling the creator/instance-creator overflow case of 18 people in an instance is accepted work but is not implemented yet. Do not rely on overflow admission for a playtest. Can I pass control of the game to someone else? Yes. Open Host , select a player, and offer Pass Host . They have 20 seconds to accept; the current host stays in control until acceptance. This transfers the game-host role, not VRChat’s instance ownership or master role. What if the host goes AFK? After five minutes without meaningful activity, another player can Claim Host . A visible/audible 20-second warning gives the host time to use Keep Hosting or resume meaningful input. If the host leaves, claiming becomes available immediately. Only one claim can be pending. The creator has tested Pass Host and AFK Claim Host in uploaded play. Less common cases such as claimant departure and simulation-owner suspension still need expanded testing. Going AFK This is different from the host claim above. Stay ready, open Host and tap AFK next round : you still ride out with the crew, but the next round's difficulty, quotas and supply count are worked out as if you were watching from dispatch, and the roster shows [AFK] next to your name. Stepping outside the van area during a round clears it on its own, as does tapping the button again. Readying up also clears AFK: if already ready, unready and then ready again. Clearing AFK during a round does not change that round's starting AFK record or commendation eligibility. If you spend an entire round inside the van area without ever stepping out, the game marks you AFK for the next round by itself and tells you on the result screen. Someone who was AFK when a round began and then comes back keeps every cash and XP reward from that round but earns no commendation for it. What else can the host do? Start ready players , Restart contract , or Cancel round / return to dispatch . Start is a click and begins the countdown; restart and cancellation retain confirmation. Restart keeps this contract’s paid claims. Cancelling preserves earnings and ends the round; the next start is a fresh contract. Ready choices persist after completion or cancellation. The host can remain unready and spectate. Why did the round start without me? Only players ready at departure join the contract. New arrivals start unready. Ready / Unready stays on until you opt out, and changes during a round apply to the next departure. See the joining rules . Why can’t I see the live field map? The dispatch map is for spectators at dispatch. Joining the crew, being downed, or waiting to enter as a participant removes the dispatch view. Crew in the field have their own map on the van's monitor: it plots the crew with their names, and the spook only during extraction or while it stands in the open near the van after someone has seen it. A missing or delayed network snapshot displays a waiting/tracking-age message. Can I watch a specific player? Yes, from dispatch on PC. Every crew dot on the dispatch map carries a name; tap the dot, the name, or the roster in the legend column, and the screen on the office window shows an over-the-shoulder view of that player. The spook can be picked too. Tap again, tap CLOSE VIEW , or walk away from dispatch to close it. Crew in the field can do the same from the van: tap a teammate on the van's monitor and the old security CRT on the driver-side wall shows them. The spook can be watched there only while the van map shows it: once you have sighted it yourself, and then only during extraction or while it stands in the open near the van. It never appears in that view before you have seen it yourself. Walking away from the van closes the view. The view is PC-only for now (the mobile builds show the names and roster but refuse the camera), and whether the watched avatar actually appears depends on your own avatar visibility settings and distance culling. Why does Tab stop me on desktop? That happened in the tested VRChat client, including another world. Use the direct keyboard shortcuts during movement. I can pin the menu for reading, but Tab is still needed for clicking. What makes a useful bug report? Tell the playtest organizer the platform, approximate time, number of players, area, spook, and what happened before the issue. Include whether you were host or spectator, a screenshot if useful, and the build being tested. Avoid posting raw client logs publicly; they can contain account or session details.

title: Your first shift
text: Your first shift Development build: art, balance, and features are still changing. Spectator radar and AI diagnostics are temporary development features, not promises for the finished game. Content warning: Contains darkness, flickering lights and sudden loud sounds (gunshots). Your job: finish the shared contract, get back to the van, then return to dispatch. Each round is one contract. Bring back orange cargo and fuel/repair green generators to finish both quotas. Contribute for the contract bonus; extract alive for more. Work rewards are kept if the contract fails, but that round's XP remains subject to extraction penalties. Remember three rewards: cash buys supplies for this live session; XP earns levels and perk points; commendations permanently unlock reusable gear. Survival points is the old name for commendations. Career titles and survivor field notes are longer-term goals you can explore after your first shift. New to the company? Read About SpookCo for the contracts, dispatch and the spooks. 1. Get ready at dispatch Wait for saved progress to load. On your first visit, choose English or Japanese; the choice is saved and can be changed under Controls → i18n / Language . This is separate from the website's language switch. New arrivals start not ready . Click Ready / Unready to opt in. Your choice stays on between rounds until you unready; Watch / Withdraw also opts out. Your button shows your own ready status alongside the shared ready count. The game host clicks Start next round with at least one player ready. A five-second countdown appears on the ready controls. Only ready players depart; the host may remain unready and spectate. Other players can click the start control to ready/unready. Its host name follows game-host transfers, independently of VRChat master status. The office Host panel also offers Start. Find Controls & Accessibility beside the ready board. Outside the roll-up door, on the right, is the free practice bay. Lit billboards stand across the low yard fence in the vacant lot, facing it. They carry full-size field and industrial generator exhibits, diagrams for all three startup games and a loadout poster (a sign over the exit points the way). These are visual references, not interactive machines, and cannot consume fuel. The practice bay has three startup tasks, free soda, tape and oil, and a crate to carry and throw. None of it touches your saved supplies or rewards. A generator you finish clears away for you until you press the Reset tutorial post by the bench twice. Leaving the bay puts the practice supplies back. 2. Read the contract Each round begins with a 15-second briefing for the contract, shop and loadout. The destination and spook are rolled for each new round. You may leave the van at any second of the briefing. Your status shows BRIEFING — shop at the van or head out (Ns) and your status readout counts down, so the crew can read the contract and shop together before heading out — or go at once. Shopping and selling at the van's side-door boards work the whole briefing; when the expedition starts those boards go blank until the next briefing. 3. Head into the field The expedition lasts 150–240 seconds depending on crew size. Briarwood High School gives every crew at least seven minutes. Carry orange cargo cases back to the van and repair green equipment. Repairs retain progress when interrupted. Every required objective can be done alone without a purchased item or specific perk. At Briarwood High School , follow the hallway loop around the courtyard and use the four marked stairs to reach the basement plant. The cafeteria, gym, auditorium, library and basement stay open at every crew size. Classrooms open in groups: 9 for 1–2 players, 18 for 3–4, 27 for 5–7, and all 36 for 8 or more. Check the ground/B1 tabs on the van map. Generators start dry. Small field generators need one can; industrial diesel generators need two. Find cans around the unlocked map and carry them against the machine: each can stays attached. Industrial controls unlock only after both cans arrive. Every round spawns two or three spare cans beyond its actual requirement. Solo and duo rounds use one small generator. Crews of 3–8 get at least one of each size; 9–12 get at least two small and one industrial; 13–16 get at least two of each. Remaining choices and their positions are randomized when the round starts. A short pole marks the machine's state: slow flashing red means empty, solid red means one of two cans, orange means startup required, and pale green means running. Minigame panels have a translucent backing so movement behind them stays visible. Use the controls on the front to complete one shuffled startup task: Prime and purge: pump until the fuel chamber fills, then bleed the trapped air. Clear three pockets and press Start Engine. Extra pumping and early bleeding make noise. Listen and tune: adjust choke and throttle until both read Steady, then press Start Engine. The sound and visual meters give the same information. Route the fuel: turn three valves to connect the top-left supply to the bottom-right engine inlet, then press Start Engine. More than one route works. The first three fueled generators draw all three games in a random order. A task stays assigned and keeps its progress when you step away. One person operates a generator at a time; someone else can take over after they leave or stop working. Mistakes attract the spook from farther away. Mechanic and tool oil make the controls more forgiving, and repair tape fixes one task step without skipping the final start. Finishing a generator also powers nearby active gear: stay within six metres with no solid wall between you and the machine to recharge twice as fast . It keeps working during extraction. The machine label and your HUD/wrist show the benefit; spooks can still reach you there. Crew at stop start Cargo Repairs 1 2 1 2 3 1 3–4 5 2 5–8 8 3 9–12 12 4 13–16 16 5 Players joining the world wait for the next round and do not raise the active quota. Departures and withdrawals can lower requirements while preserving finished work. Downed players and teammates sheltering at the van still count. The field is not the same twice. Every stop rolls fresh obstacles — hay bales, broken-down vehicles, fallen trees, crates and drums — alongside the usual random supplies, and worksite front doors can be opened and closed while you work. See know the spooks for how the spook deals with a door you shut behind you. 4. Regroup and extract The covered campfire refuge beside the van is protected throughout the stop. Enter and leave freely. You can walk into the van through its side opening, the back or a cab door (click a cab door's handle or window to open or close it); the bench, console and doors inside do not block you, and the van is part of the protected refuge. Finishing the quota starts extraction early, with 60–90 seconds depending on the crew-size tier, or at least 90 seconds at Briarwood . Running out of expedition time triggers emergency extraction instead. Get back before departure: it does not wait indefinitely for missing players. Transit takes 10 seconds : the view fades to black over one second and stays dark with a short next-stop message while walking pauses, then fades in at the next van. Standing avatars are never driven around. Menus cannot be opened during transit. The crew arrives spread around the van on separate spots rather than stacked on one point, and the same applies whenever the game moves you — a restart, a recovery, or returning to dispatch. After a completed contract, gold-strapped BONUS SALVAGE cases become available near the van's surrounding work area: one for an initial crew of 1–2, two for 3–8, or three for 9–16. Bring them back using the normal cargo controls. Each pays double normal cargo XP and $24 , and a real handoff shares credit. They are optional and never raise the required quota. The extraction clock keeps running. The crew gets an eight-second decision window before the usual all-aboard departure check starts; everyone can stay aboard and skip the salvage. Unfinished bonus cases never hold the van past its deadline. Failed contracts unlock no bonus work, and restarting a stop never replenishes a bonus case that already paid. Missing extraction keeps only 10% of your round XP. Each dispatched player left behind also reduces everyone's round XP by 10%, capped at 50%; previous rounds' XP stays untouched. One completed contract finishes the round. A short result shows the outcome and your cash, XP and commendations, then everyone returns to dispatch. Staying safe without contributing does not earn the contract bonus. Players who remain ready join the next round when the host starts it. Lethal attacks Roadkill's charge, warned catches from Hitchhiker and Usher, and gunshots from Warden and Deadeye eliminate you for the rest of the round, even with Hardhat or Second Wind. You drop what you are carrying and can spectate at dispatch. If everyone is eliminated, the stop ends promptly. Your banked rewards remain. See spook counterplay for warnings and escape routes. If you go down You normally start with two health. A short immunity interval prevents immediate repeated hits. Going down puts you on the floor: you crawl slowly, you cannot jump, and you drop whatever you were carrying. Your first down of a stop gives you 20 seconds ; every later down in the same stop gives you 10. Getting within 2 metres of a downed teammate automatically starts rescuing them. Stay within 4 metres to continue; each rescuer helps one teammate at a time. It works with cargo or equipment in hand and with menus open, without pressing a button. One rescuer takes 10 seconds , and each extra rescuer takes a quarter off that — 7.5 seconds for two, 5.6 for three. Field Medic halves the crew's time. Your bleed-out countdown stops while anyone contributes. Leaving range resumes the countdown immediately; rescue progress survives for 2.5 seconds , then resets and adds half the invested time back to the countdown. Camp-AFK teammates can rescue you too; suspended players cannot. If no able teammate remains, including solo play, your countdown is cut to a few seconds rather than run in full — nothing can answer it, but you still get that long on the floor. Otherwise, when your countdown expires, what happens depends on when you went down. In the first half of a stop an eight-second recovery brings you round at the nearest recovery stone in your ring — a small glowing gravestone — when it is closer than the van, otherwise at the van. The stones vanish at the halfway point and take nobody after it. After halfway you are out for the rest of that stop: you return to dispatch, can watch the live field map, and join the next host-started round if you remain ready. Dropped cargo can be recovered either way. Capture never removes banked XP or commendations. Second Wind allows a six-second field recovery on the first ordinary down of a stop; it cannot revive an elimination. Joining a round already in progress New arrivals stay at dispatch and start unready. Ready / Unready during a round sets your choice for the next departure; it does not join or withdraw you from the active contract. Unreadying in the field lets you finish this round and sit out the next. Your ready choice lasts until you change it or leave the instance. Continue with controls , equipment , and spook counterplay .

title: Progression & saving
text: Progression & saving The save system is implemented, but reconnect and multi-instance edge cases still need expanded uploaded testing. Do not treat a development build as a permanent economy guarantee. What stays with you Resource Purpose Intended lifetime XP Levels and perk-point capacity Permanent across visits Commendations Lifetime equipment milestones; never spent Permanent across visits Career mastery Job and spook ranks; cosmetic crew titles Permanent across visits Cash Buy consumables The live instance session Consumable pouch Purchased and scavenged supplies The live instance session Build and controls Perk/equipment choices and device preferences Saved across visits Rejoining the same live session is designed to restore cash, pouch contents, and relevant equipment state. A → B → A uses separate records while A remains live. Up to 128 recent sessions are retained. When everyone leaves, that session ends; a later fresh session begins with fresh cash and supplies. Wait for restoration before shopping or collecting. Accepted changes are saved during play, not just on departure. A sudden crash can lose the most recent cloud write. Capture does not remove banked XP or commendations. Earn your contract bonus Moving around or waiting in the van does not count as work. Contribute by delivering cargo, bringing fuel to a generator, completing or meaningfully helping a repair, rescuing a teammate, or using gear to interrupt an active chase or warning. Result XP Cash Commendations A contract your crew completes and you contributed to 25 10 1 You also extract alive from that completed contract 15 5 1 more Failed contract, even if you reach the van No round bonus No round bonus 0 You did not contribute No round bonus No round bonus 0 Round XP is provisional until extraction. Failing to extract keeps only 10% of your earned round XP. Every dispatched player who fails to extract also reduces everyone's round XP by 10%, capped at 50%. Apply the personal reduction first, then the crew reduction, and round the final total down. A player who misses extraction with one crew member missing keeps 9%; with five or more missing, they keep 5%. A player who extracts with two missing keeps 80%. Only the current round's XP is reduced. Previously banked XP, cash and commendations are untouched. The dispatched roster includes disconnected players; spectators and later arrivals do not add penalties. A failed contract provides no contract or extraction bonus. If you contributed and the crew completes the contract after you are eliminated, its XP bonus is included in the reduced total. Cancelling a live contract settles it as a failed extraction. Cargo and repair finishers earn 10 / 12 / 20 / 30 XP for an initial crew of 1–2 / 3–4 / 5–8 / 9+ respectively. Cargo pays $8, repair pays $12, and fully fueling a generator pays $4 with the same crew-scaled XP. A player who supplies the first can to a two-can generator receives helper credit when a teammate supplies the second. Scrapper increases objective cash by 20%. Optional bonus salvage unlocks only after the required contract is complete. Its finisher earns 20 / 24 / 40 / 60 XP for the same initial-crew brackets and $24 per case. Qualified handoff helpers receive half; Scrapper applies normally. Cash is awarded on delivery; the XP remains subject to extraction penalties. There are only one to three bonus cases per stop, and each pays once per trip, including restarts. A cargo helper must carry the case at least three metres before handing it off. A repair helper must supply at least 10% of the completed repair. Qualified helpers receive half the objective XP and cash when someone finishes the task. Picking up and dropping a case or tapping a generator is not enough. Restarting a stop does not pay the same objective again. Rescue credit is bounded to 10 XP / $3 per rescuer per stop. Gear that successfully interrupts an active threat can grant 8 XP / $3 once per stop; repeatedly distracting an idle spook grants nothing. Each round ends after one contract. There is no additional three-stop shift payout. Contribute to a completed contract and extract alive to earn 40 base XP, $15 and 2 commendations , on top of your completed work rewards. The XP total still receives any crew extraction penalty. The result screen shows your outcome, total cash, XP and commendations, then the return-to-dispatch countdown. Each reward line explains its use. The menu keeps the work, contract and extraction breakdown and next equipment unlock. Commendations is the current name for survival points; existing balances retain their value and are never spent. Career mastery and titles Open Perks , page past Specialist perks and More perks , then choose Career mastery . Two career pages show your counts, next rank and title choices. Select an earned title to display it beside your name in the crew roster, or choose No title to hide it. Titles automatically show your current rank, I, II or III. They are cosmetic and give no combat advantage. Track What counts Rank I / II / III Hauler Paid cargo deliveries, including bonus salvage and qualified handoff assists 5 / 25 / 100 Engineer Paid generator fuel and completed repairs, including qualified repair assists 5 / 25 / 100 Crew Support Paid rescues and useful gear support; each category counts once per stop 5 / 25 / 100 Each of the ten spooks Contribute to a completed contract and extract alive from that spook 3 / 10 / 25 Finishing work and meaningfully helping earn equal mastery credit, even though helper XP and cash are smaller. Merely surviving, failing the contract or missing extraction gives no spook mastery. Restarting the same stop cannot repeat its paid mastery. Job progress already earned survives a failed stop. Older records that remember surviving a spook begin with one proven escape for that spook. They cannot reconstruct old job counts. Mastery and title selection save with your permanent profile. Levels and perk points Start at level 1 with 2 points . Gain a point at levels 2, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 28, 32, 36 and 40 , reaching 15 points at level 40 . The early gains let you afford a four-point perk at level 3. Choose any combination of unique perks within your budget and respec freely during briefings. Perk Cost Current effect Spotter 1 Objective markers visible 50% farther away Courier 2 Removes the cargo movement penalty Mechanic 2 Stronger primer strokes, forgiving engine tuning, and a highlighted break in the fuel route Field Medic 2 Halves the required revive time Scrapper 2 20% more objective cash Soft Soles 3 Movement hearing range reduced by 25% Adrenaline 3 Extraction movement bonus Quickdraw 3 Active equipment cooldowns reduced by 20% Hardhat 4 One extra maximum health; does not protect against lethal attacks Second Wind 4 Six-second field recovery on first ordinary down each stop; cannot reverse elimination Silent Tools 2 Level 3: halves repair noise range; footsteps are unchanged Ear Defenders 2 Level 3: halves howl slow duration; does not affect fog Escape Artist 4 Level 10: partial peeks take longer to confirm and visual searches last 35% less time; hearing still matters Braced 3 Level 6: 15% faster sideways movement for dodging; no lethal-hit immunity Clear Lenses 2 Level 6: reduces hazard fog density by 35%; ordinary world fog remains Sixth Sense 3 Level 9: HUD warning when a nearby spook winds up an attack, within 25 m Trailbreaker 3 Level 12: searches based on your footsteps last 35% less time; sight is unchanged Inspector 2 Level 3: identifies the nearest visible, unclaimed field supply within 8 m Focused Beam 3 Level 15: a narrower flashlight beam that reaches about two thirds farther; its switch is quiet and spooks never hear it. The Usher and Deadeye can still see the beam The three-page perk menu shows cost, required level and equipped state. The original ten perks have no extra level requirement. Saved affordable builds keep their selections. Combined gear and perk movement bonuses are capped at 20%; Sprint soda's 30% adds on top, and Braced separately improves sideways movement by 15%. Perks support different roles; required tasks remain possible with the starter loadout. XP comes from completed work, bounded rescue/support credit, contributed contract and extraction results. Idle waiting, movement alone, and supply collection do not generate XP. The early level curve stays unchanged through level 10. Each subsequent level costs the base amount ( 150 + 35 × (current level − 1) ) multiplied by the current band: Current level XP cost multiplier 1–9 1× 10–14 2× 15–19 5× 20–24 12× 25–29 16× 30–34 20× 35–39 24× Level 10 requires 2,610 banked XP, level 15 7,960 , level 20 25,710 , and level 40 456,310 . Perk-point milestones stay spaced across those levels; the budget still caps at 15. Later permanent equipment requires both a level and commendation milestone. Actual days or hours to reach these milestones depend on contributions and extraction success and need live balance data.

title: Know the spooks
text: Know the spooks One spook is active at a time. Melee spooks keep pace with a running employee and gain speed with larger crews. Warden and Deadeye move more slowly, but threaten firing lanes at a distance. Read the warning and use each spook's recovery window. Spook What it does What to try Groundskeeper Sight pursuit, remembered routes, and local searches Break sight, change route, and quietly leave its search area. Rattletrap Blind; investigates movement and task noise Walk when possible, time repairs, and use a decoy. Roadkill Telegraphs a lethal, committed charge Dodge sideways and put solid cover between you and its line. Hitchhiker Ambushes from concealed positions; warned catches are lethal Watch roadside silhouettes and change approach. Usher Warns before a lethal chase from its vision cone; drawn to flashlight beams it can see Get out of the cone or behind cover before the lock completes. Switch your light off when it is near. Switchboard Pursues and marks work-site/route hazards Leave the marked area and switch sites. Hound Follows aging movement trails as well as sight Creep, double back, and leave the old trail behind. Trailbreaker helps. Mimic Disguises itself as false cargo, then warns before revealing Watch for eyes, twitching and creaks. Back away; Inspector can identify it. Warden Warns, commits to a shotgun fan, fires, then reloads Leave the fan or reach solid cover. Move while it reloads. Deadeye Quickly confirms sight, raises its rifle with a warning sound, commits and fires; spots flashlight beams from far away Break sight immediately or sidestep before the shot. It changes position between shots. Keep your beam out of its view. Your footsteps matter Creeping is quiet for ordinary spooks. Footsteps grow louder gradually as you move faster, and solid cover greatly reduces their reach. Rattletrap is the hearing specialist: it can detect slower movement and hear more through cover. Running is much riskier than walking. Soft Soles reduces movement hearing ranges by 25%. A brief head-only or body-only peek builds suspicion before a sighted spook confirms you. Repeated peeks accumulate suspicion, and showing both your head and torso confirms you immediately. Once a spook is tracking you, a currently visible head or torso is enough to maintain a recent chase. Full cover still breaks sight, and cover does not erase a route the spook already saw. This senses in-game movement and certain task events. It does not listen to microphone audio or voice chat. Flashlights Switching a flashlight makes a click that a spook within earshot hears, much like a footstep, and solid cover muffles it. Switch in cover or away from the spook. The Usher and Deadeye also notice a lit beam they can see: the patch of wall or floor it lights, or the lamp itself pointed their way. They come for whoever holds it. A passing glimpse is not enough, but a beam that stays in their view for a moment is. Focused Beam 's switch is silent to spooks, but its beam is still light. Hiding in shrubs Dense shrubs conceal you from ordinary spook vision and reduce your walking, running and sideways movement speed by 50% while your body is inside. Leaving restores your normal speed. The slowdown stacks with carried cargo, perks and temporary effects. Break sight before entering. A spook actively chasing or aiming at you can keep tracking you if it watches you enter. If you break its view, the shrub conceals you until you expose yourself or it comes over to inspect your hiding place. Standing on top of foliage does not count as hiding. Keep your flashlight off or pointed away from the spook. A head lamp or hand light shining directly at a sighted spook reveals you through foliage when you are within its view and range. Once it sees you, switching the light off alone does not hide you again: break its sight. Solid cover and smoke still conceal you, and Rattletrap remains blind. A bush can be searched. After losing you in a chase, a spook checks nearby bushes around the route or open area it reached. It walks over and pauses to inspect them; a sighted spook can discover you when it looks into your bush at close range. It can check empty bushes too, and still gives up when its search expires. Watch where it goes and quietly move away before it checks your hiding place. Bushes do not suppress hearing, erase Hound trails, stop committed bullets or charges, or make you invulnerable. Rattletrap remains a hearing specialist. Quiet movement and a route change still matter. Cars, trailers, equipment and wooden fences provide solid cover. Chain-link fencing blocks passage while allowing sight through it; plan around its openings. One corner is not a guaranteed escape A spook that has seen you commits to you. For as long as the commitment lasts it sees you farther and wider, hears your footsteps and your flashlight click through cover, and prefers you over a teammate who happens to be nearer. When you break its sight it does not stop at the corner: it runs to where it last saw you, then around the turn your route was taking, and only after that does it search, quickly and at full pace, around that corner. Keep running after the turn and your footsteps re-aim it. It never knows where you actually are once you are out of sight; it guesses from the way you were going and from what it can hear. It tires. About 20 to 32 seconds after its last sighting, depending on the spook, with every sound of yours pushing that a few seconds further, it gives up, recovers, and goes back to its rounds. Warden and Deadeye commit too; Rattletrap commits to the first footsteps it locates; the Hound follows your scent around the corner. Quietly escaping still works: creep, take a second turn it did not see, or double back, and let it tire. Escape Artist shortens a commitment made by sight; Trailbreaker shortens one made by sound and makes Hound trails fade sooner. The refuge and a decoy end it outright; a stun or a flash only interrupts it. An uncommitted search (from a noise it heard, say) is shorter and slower than a committed one. Break sight, change route, reduce noise, and use the protected refuge when needed. Sound gives the AI an investigation point; it is not treated as direct vision through a wall. Running in a straight line is unreliable against melee spooks. They lead their turns instead of trailing you, and inside about three metres they can lunge. A landed hit costs them a moment's recovery, which is the gap you use to reach cover, a door or the van. Carrying a case slows you below their pace: drop it if you are being run down. Reaching the van ends the hunt Make it into the van's protected area with a spook behind you and it gives up on you. Within a moment it turns away from the camp and heads back out into the field, searching as it goes: anyone it spots or hears out there is fair game, and that is who it chases next. For about 15 seconds after you get in, anyone within about 12 m of the camp, roughly the edge of the lantern's glow, goes unnoticed and cannot be struck, so the crew can regroup and step straight back out. Farther out you are fair game as usual. Spooks do not loiter at the camp. Their rounds and searches never stop inside the lantern's glow, and for about a minute after an escape their rounds keep well clear of the van. They still come close when they are chasing someone they can see or hear, and a teammate downed near the van is left after a short look, so they can be rescued. Lethal attacks Roadkill's charge, a warned catch from Hitchhiker or Usher, and a hit from Warden or Deadeye eliminate you for the rest of the round. Hardhat and Second Wind cannot save you from these attacks. Spawn and rescue immunity still protect you. Hitchhiker and Usher must warn before committing; breaking sight cancels their lethal chase, and they must warn again for a full two seconds when they find you again, even mid-chase. A missed commitment gives you a recovery window. Solid cover stops contact through walls. You can spectate from dispatch, and you join the next host-started round if you remain ready. If the whole crew is eliminated, the stop ends promptly. Eliminated players do not reduce the required task quota, and reconnecting or toggling readiness does not undo elimination. Reading a gun warning React to the raised weapon and warning sound immediately. Both gun spooks now acquire and fire quickly, with no visible aiming rays or shot tracers. Their aim follows you briefly, then fixes before firing: a late sidestep can still avoid the shot. Solid cover blocks the actual shot, including after commitment. Smoke can break acquisition or an uncommitted aim, but it cannot stop a bullet already aimed at your position. Decoys redirect an uncommitted armed spook; they cannot cancel its warning once aiming starts. A successful flash or trip alarm interrupts it and makes it confirm you again. Warden must reload after its shotgun blast. Deadeye reloads and looks for a new firing position. Neither deals melee contact damage. False cargo and old trails Mimic cargo is separate from real objectives. It never takes away delivered work. Its breathing, eyes and twitch are clues before the reveal; Inspector identifies a nearby visible disguise. Smoke can conceal your approach, and the reveal warning gives you time to back away. The Hound follows recorded movement only after a delay. Quiet creeping leaves no new trail; old samples expire instead of tracking your hidden position. It can still see you normally, so use cover as you leave the trail. Doors, and a field that changes every stop Worksite front doors can be opened and closed. Shut one behind you and the spook has to deal with it: an unhurried one opens it, but a spook that is chasing you breaks it off its hinge , and a broken door cannot be closed again. A door buys you distance once, so spend it well. Nobody can close a door on a person standing in the doorway, and the rear opening of every worksite stays clear so you are never sealed in. The field itself is rolled again at the start of every stop: hay bales, broken-down vehicles, fallen trees, crates, oil drums and more appear in different places, alongside the usual random supplies. Learn the landmarks, not the route. Spectating the current build Choose Watch / Withdraw to remain at dispatch. The Live Field Map shows crew and spook tracking, with every crew member named beside their dot. In the current test build, a gold outline depicts vision and blue rings depict walking/running hearing; Rattletrap has hearing only. The dispatch map always plots the spook for spectators, before the crew has identified it. Tap a name, a dot, the spook arrow or the roster in the legend column and the screen on the office window follows that player or the spook over the shoulder (PC only for now). The crew's own van map plots teammates by name too, but shows the spook only during extraction or in the open near the van after a sighting. Tap a teammate on the van map and the security CRT on the van's driver-side wall follows them the same way (PC only for now); the spook appears in that view only while the van map shows it. Development feature: visible sensing radar and AI diagnostics may change or disappear from the final game. The map is a simplified horizontal view, not a guarantee of detection at every height or through every shape of cover.

title: SpookCo: Last Stop
text: The night shift has a survival clause. Take the company van into the dark. Recover cargo, patch up the equipment, and get everyone back to the campfire lantern before departure. Something out there heard you clock in. Content warning: Contains darkness, flickering lights and sudden loud sounds (gunshots). Spookality 2026: SpookCo: Last Stop has been submitted. Development continues after submission, with further updates to the playable world as features and fixes are ready. One contract. Get the crew home. SpookCo: Last Stop is a cooperative horror world built around short expeditions and a dependable refuge. Play alone or bring a crew of up to 16. Finish the work, scavenge what you can, and decide when to make a run for the van. Clock in Ready up at dispatch, choose your equipment, and read the contract. Stay ready for future rounds; the host starts each departure. Do the work Recover cargo and repair equipment. Field supplies are shared: whoever collects a pickup gets it. Running is faster, but it carries farther through the dark. Make it back The van’s covered campfire refuge stays safe. Complete the quota to open extraction early, or scramble aboard during emergency extraction. Departure has a deadline. A small world with a long night ahead Contracts use the authored destinations: Camp Deadwood , Last Chance Service Station , Calder laboratory , and Briarwood High School . Ten spooks use different senses and attack patterns. Some follow movement noise or old trails; others disguise themselves or warn before a lethal charge, catch, or gunshot. Quiet movement, cover, doors and knowing when to move matter. Required work earns rewards and opens extraction. Once the contract is complete, optional bonus salvage offers more XP and cash within the existing departure deadline. Repaired generators recharge nearby active gear faster. Nineteen perks, ten consumables, five reusable tools and persistent job/spook mastery provide choices across shifts; standing around to survive does not earn a round bonus. This is a playable build still early in development , and it may change significantly after the game jam . Gameplay, progression, maps, and art are all subject to change. The local expansion includes dressed maps, darker dispatch lighting, distance fog and a glowing lounge CRT. Balance, device performance and multiplayer edge cases still need playtesting. Spectator sensing radar and AI diagnostics remain development tools and may change before release. Your first shift Start with the quick-start guide , check your controls , or learn what to pack in the equipment guide . The site describes the current baseline; an older uploaded build may behave differently. New to the company? Read About SpookCo for the contracts, dispatch and the spooks. A catnet systems production, created by kittyn . Meet the creator and view the credits →
